solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Got key cut

parts.note: F is a musical key
to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: Someone had a new key cut at the locksmith's.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetched and got both mean went for and brought back, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Walton's deceptive appearance?

definitions.meaning: the English composer William Walton wrote an entertainment of poems set to music under this title
a false front that hides the truth

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man called Walton is putting on an act.
explanation.walkthrough: Walton here is the composer William Walton, whose 1922 piece set Edith Sitwell's poems.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's front, and figuratively a false outward show hiding reality.

clue.text: Transposing the bookmaker's sign language is part of the strategy

indicators.note: transposing means swapping the two halves of the term so the end moves to the front

parts.note: tic-tac is the hand-signal system used by British racecourse bookmakers

explanation.surface: Swapping bookies' hand signals is part of a betting plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transposing' swaps the two halves of TIC-TAC to give TAC then TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A single manoeuvre or move is one component of an overall plan.

clue.text: Lead, say, in hard rock

definitions.meaning: lead is an example of a dense, weighty element such as lead or uranium
a loud, aggressive style of rock music

explanation.surface: Lead is found in hard rock, as an ore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' wants to be the verb or a leading role; it is the dense element.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense elements like lead and the loud guitar music genre share this name.

clue.text: The last place to fight?

parts.note: from the idiom of a last-... stand, a final defensive trench

explanation.surface: Asks where a final battle should be fought.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench dug for defence, as in making a last-ditch stand.

clue.text: Drew the card out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the card are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A player pulled a card from the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew' looks like drawing a card; it is the definition, as in drew a map.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart a coastline is to draw it on a map, so drew is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Proved to be a full member of the church

definitions.text: to be a full member of the church
definitions.meaning: admitted to full church membership through the rite of confirmation

explanation.surface: Someone has shown they really belong in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Verified as true, and having undergone the Christian rite admitting full membership.

clue.text: They go round in circles

parts.note: suggests people getting nowhere, but means curved segments lying on a circle's edge

explanation.surface: Some people keep going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved sections of a circumference are parts of circles.

clue.text: Hot work during Test that contains century

indicators.note: during puts the work piece inside the test piece
that contains puts the century piece inside the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Hard work during a cricket Test match in which someone scores a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match and a century is 100 runs, but here TRIAL and C.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot, humid climate near the equator is described this way.

clue.text: Reveal record to be unsuccessful

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
to lose is to be unsuccessful

explanation.surface: Reveal that a record has flopped.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose and to reveal both mean to make known.

clue.text: Two officers get together with a drink

indicators.note: two asks for the officers piece to be given twice over

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer

explanation.surface: A pair of officers meet up for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate made with powdered cacao is a familiar milky drink.

clue.text: Firm can set out to restrict debt

indicators.note: to restrict means to hem in, so the debt piece sits inside the rearranged letters
set out tells the solver to lay the letters of can set out afresh

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgment of a debt

explanation.surface: A company can arrange to limit its borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun beside 'can set'; it is the adjective meaning resolute. 'out' rearranges CAN SET to TENACS before 'to restrict' acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of unyielding and resolute matches holding on stubbornly.

clue.text: A succession of small bloomers

parts.note: bloomers suggests underwear blunders, but means little flowers linked one after another in a garland

explanation.surface: A run of minor mistakes or a line of tiny knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Children thread small field flowers stem to stem into a linked garland.

clue.text: Appears as laid back, but is on watch

indicators.note: laid back is read as the word laid turned backwards

explanation.surface: Someone seems relaxed, yet is actually on sentry duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' looks like relaxed; 'back' turns LAID round. 'on watch' looks like guard duty but means found on a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a wristwatch showing the hours is its numbered face plate.

clue.text: Teaches a number limited by English, perhaps

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in by, so the number sits inside the other letters
perhaps signals that the letters of English are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A teacher conveys a number, constrained by the English language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English, perhaps' reads as an example of a language; 'perhaps' actually rearranges its letters to ENLIGHS, which 'limited by' then wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone knowledge or understanding is to instruct them.

clue.text: They recommend its men to sail abroad

indicators.note: abroad, meaning scattered widely, signals the letters of its men to sail being mixed

explanation.surface: Sailors are commended for going overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: References or letters of commendation are written to recommend a person.

clue.text: A piece of light music?

parts.note: light music suggests easy listening, but read literally a song about a flame or lamp

explanation.surface: Asks for an easy-listening tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental ballad of unrequited love, punning on a flaming torch as light.

clue.text: A swimmer has first to get changed

indicators.note: get changed asks for the letters of has first to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A swimmer is first into the changing room.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-armed sea creature moving through the water is a marine swimmer.

clue.text: Sort of key that may be found in a cupboard?

definitions.meaning: a master key that opens many locks

definitions.text: that may be found in a cupboard?
definitions.meaning: from the idiom of a shameful secret

explanation.surface: Asks about a kind of key you might keep in a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key, and the bony frame hidden in a cupboard as a secret.

clue.text: Receive satisfaction from supply to Longleat?

definitions.meaning: to be proud of something you have done
Longleat is an English stately home with a safari park famed for lions, so delivering a group of lions there

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys delivering goods to a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of lions is a pride; Longleat, in Wiltshire, England, has a well-known lion enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being proud of one's work is an idiom for feeling satisfaction in it.

clue.text: Musician puts sheet on piano? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary reverses the order stated, so piano goes on top of sheet

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
a sheet is a layer

explanation.surface: A musician lays a dust sheet over the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says sheet on piano; 'On the contrary' flips that, so in this down answer P sits above LAYER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays an instrument is a performer of music.

clue.text: Separated and left

explanation.surface: A couple split up and went away.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided apart, and also went away, as in parted company.

clue.text: Bread from trolley

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the inside of the word trolley

explanation.surface: Fetch a bun from the food trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: A small individually baked bread piece is a common kind of bun.

clue.text: It's cold in the country — you need a fur

indicators.note: in places the cold piece inside the country's name

parts.note: China is a country in Asia
a chill is a cold feeling

explanation.surface: It's freezing in that land, so you'll want a fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey pelt of a small South American rodent is prized for coats.

clue.text: Donne has been translated quite a lot

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters of Donne being converted into another form

explanation.surface: The poet John Donne has been widely translated.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne is the English metaphysical poet, but here only five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a great deal, as in it cheered me up immensely.

clue.text: Short game in which a child goes to sleep

definitions.text: in which a child goes to sleep

explanation.surface: A quick game played while the baby naps.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for cribbage, a card game, and a baby's cot.

clue.text: Put in for one stripe during manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests the letters of one stripe being moved around into new positions

explanation.surface: A soldier is recommended for a single stripe during army exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something between other things or to interject a remark is to insert it.

clue.text: GP yet to be reappointed to African country

indicators.note: reappointed suggests the letters of GP yet being put back in new places

explanation.surface: A family doctor is to be posted again to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation on the Nile in north-east Africa, home of the pyramids.

clue.text: Most women have this combination of give and take

parts.note: to hand something is to give it
to bag something is to take or seize it

explanation.surface: A trait most women share is a mix of generosity and grabbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a character trait; 'Most women have this' points to an accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse carried for personal items is something most women own.

clue.text: Wanted to see knight in action

indicators.note: in places the knight piece inside the action piece

parts.note: a deed is an action
Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Someone longed to watch a knight in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanted and longed for are synonyms for something craved.
